rows.comment: An en dash stands in for 'to'. Write the word.
rows.replacement:
'Your band was off your wrist from ${_clock(bestStart)} to '
'${_clock(bestEnd)}.'
lineComments: Replace the en dash with 'from ... to'.

rows.comment: 'What normal looks like for you' is a roundabout way to say baseline.
rows.replacement: 'Not enough history to set your baseline yet.'
lineComments: Name the missing thing, the baseline.

rows.comment: Awkward subject; say who has no record.
rows.replacement: 'The app has no record of why this is missing.'
lineComments: Name the actor and state the fact.

rows.comment: States why no trend is shown.
lineComments: Gives the reason for the missing trend.

rows.comment: Accessibility label assembled from data; no prose problems.
Screen-reader label that reads the card's parts in order.
Button label says what it opens.
Error states the problem and the outcome.

Chart legend label for screen readers; fragment of an expression.
Tells the reader what is shown and what tapping does.
Em dash, 'not X, not Y' antithesis. Keep the fact that the stream is not saved (live streams are RAM-only) and state it once.
rows.replacement:
'The last ${trace.length} readings, ${trace.reduce(math.min)}'
' to ${trace.reduce(math.max)} bpm. The live stream is not saved.'
lineComments: Replace the em dash with a comma.
Range reads 'to' instead of an en dash; keep the unit.
Say once that the stream is not saved; drop the contrast with a record of the day.

rows.comment: Tells the reader where to pair.
Em dash and vague 'open link'. Name the mechanism: the app connects when opened with the band in range.
rows.replacement:
'The app connects when you open it with the band in range. '
'Live beats need that connection.'
lineComments: Lead with what the app does.
State the dependency in plain words.

rows.comment: Gives the two conditions for streaming.
Cute title that says nothing about what the card is.
rows.replacement: 'OpenStrap Discord'

rows.comment: Em dash, list of three, and 'hang out' filler. Say what people do there.
rows.replacement:
'Report bugs and ask other people running the same band '
'on the OpenStrap Discord.'
lineComments: Drop the triad and the em dash; state the actions.

rows.comment: Fishes for a feeling; name the ask.
rows.replacement: 'Support OpenStrap'
lineComments: State what the card is about.

rows.comment: 'Keeps it maintained' is vague. Keep the checkable facts: free, open source, no subscription.
rows.replacement:
'OpenStrap is free and open source, with no subscription. '
'Sponsorships fund ongoing maintenance.'

rows.comment: Passive second sentence; name the actor.
rows.replacement:
'The app opens without a band. It records nothing until '
'you pair one.'

rows.comment: Fine instruction, but the curly apostrophe should be straight.
rows.replacement:
"Take the band off the charger, put it on your wrist and keep the "
"phone within arm's reach."
lineComments: Replace the curly apostrophe with a straight one.

rows.comment: 'Up to half a minute' has no backing in the repo; the only timing note is for heart-rate sensors (15 s scan window in hrs_link.dart, 'several seconds'). Drop the number.
rows.replacement:
'A band that just came off the charger can take a while to '
'show up in the scan.'
lineComments: 'Advertising' is jargon; say it appears in the scan.

rows.comment: Say the conditions directly without jargon.
rows.replacement:
'No band answered the scan. A band shows up only when it is '
'awake and not connected to another phone.'

rows.comment: 'Almost always' is an unbacked frequency and 'rather than a fault in the band' rebuts a worry nobody raised. State the cause and the fix.
rows.replacement:
'The band rejected the encryption key. An old pairing record '
'on this phone causes this. Forget the band in Bluetooth '
'settings, then scan again.'
lineComments: Says what happened, in plain words.
Names the cause without a probability claim.

rows.comment: Counts the list in the title and sets up a reveal. Title the topic.
rows.replacement: 'Why the band does not answer'

rows.comment: Semicolon list with repeated 'it is'. Tighten.
rows.replacement:
'The band is on the charger, out of range, or connected to '
'another phone or the vendor app.'

rows.comment: Curly apostrophe, and the last sentence is awkward. State the cause and who can clear it.
rows.replacement:
"Open the phone's Bluetooth settings, forget the band, then "
"scan again here. The old pairing record caused the refused "
"key, and only the system can clear it."
lineComments: Names the cause and the limit on the app.

rows.comment: 'Normally works' is a vague success claim with no backing in the repo. Give the instruction.
rows.replacement: 'Scan again with the band about a metre from the phone.'
lineComments: Turn the claim into a step.

rows.comment: 'Four numbers' is wrong (sex is one of the four) and unnamed. List the fields and say what a blank does.
rows.replacement:
'Sex, age, height and weight change how your data is scored. '
'If you leave one blank, only the metrics that need it are unavailable.'

rows.comment: 'Published sets' points at nothing. The repo names Banister TRIMP for strain and training load; the calories constants are not named in the strings. Name the model and the fallback.
rows.replacement:
'Calories average the male and female constants. Training load '
'and strain use Banister TRIMP, which has only a male and a '
'female set, so they use the male constants.'
lineComments: States how calories are computed for this choice.
